newsitem.title: USA: Miami Airport expects Apr China Air cargo flights.
newsitem.headline: Miami Airport expects Apr China Air cargo flights.

text.p: Miami International Airport (MIA) expects Taiwan's China Airlines to be flying Taipei-Miami Boeing 747 freighter services by early April, a top MIA official said.
These will link the booming trade markets of Asia and Latin America, said Peter Reaveley, MIA's director of route development.
"It is incredibly positive for Miami. It will be bringing more freight," he added.
The new Asia-Miami-Latin America link is possible as a result of open-skies agreements between the United States and Taiwan signed in Washington last week, Reaveley said.
Reaveley was a delegate to the open-skies negotiations, which concluded "at 2 am Friday morning".

China Airlines (CAL) will be just the first to launch freighter services from Asia to Latin America's U.S. gateway of Miami, he said, adding it is expected that others will follow as Asia tries to broaden growing trade between Latin America and Asia.
The U.S. has also negotiated open-skies agreements with Singapore and Brunei and a deal is expected soon with Malaysia, Reaveley said.
But Taiwan, CAL's home, is rated as a 'Category 2' country on aviation safety by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration.

As such, CAL will not be able to use its own aircraft to fly into Miami and will instead be required to lease aircraft -- including crew and maintainence -- from a 'Category 1' country, probably the U.S.
The open-skies agreement with Taiwan will become effective in about 30 days, Reaveley said.

Reaveley said the Asia-Miami connection will be a boon for MIA's cargo carriers because China Airlines will make Miami its terminal point for what is expected to be a booming trade with Latin America.

Despite some fears that CAL might become a competitor on Latin American routes, Reaveley said the airline would tranfer freight to MIA-based cargo carriers at Miami for onward flights to Latin America.
